reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus publishes 116 MW of IT capacity across three buildings, the largest single reported figure among Virginia facilities tracked here and representing just under half of all Virginia megawatts collected from operator spec pages.

The 116 MW figure is power delivered to equipment, not total facility draw. At commonly assumed densities for AI training, 116 MW would support roughly 2,900 racks; at densities for mixed enterprise load, roughly 11,600 racks. CyrusOne publishes neither rack count nor target density, so these are illustrative calculations only, not operator claims.

Sterling sits in Northern Virginia, the densest data center market in the United States, but this data does not include grid constraints, utility relationships, or power availability specific to this location. The absence of published certifications means this facility's qualification for regulated or sensitive workloads cannot be determined from operator disclosures. A reader evaluating AI relevance should treat 116 MW as a floor on capacity and seek utility and operator information beyond these published facts for anything more.
